_README: EVERY SENTENCE THE TAPE CAN EMIT IS IN THIS FILE.
It is data, not code: edit a phrase here and the tape says the new thing
on the next load, with no logic touched. tests/test_page_language.py
scans this file directly, so the whole vocabulary is checked in one pass
rather than being hunted through render functions.
THE RULE EVERY PHRASE OBEYS: the percentage already says WHAT happened.
A phrase must carry what the percentage cannot -- an event, a level, a
volume, a position in the day. Never a restatement ('closed down'), never
a verdict ('strong', 'looks good'). Naming an event is reporting; ranking a
VARIANTS exist because repetition reads as a template. Friday put 26
volume items on a 73-item tape; one phrasing would have made a third of
the tape one sentence. They are chosen in rotation, not at random, so the
same inputs always render the same text and a screenshot can be checked.
{n} is substituted with the measurement. {minute} is substituted only
while the session is live; on a finished session the time is noise.

thresholds._move_pct: A stock needs this move AND a second fact. Lower than the 3% it replaced because the fact is the filter: a 52-week high on a 1.8% move beats a 3% move with nothing behind it.
thresholds._min_turnover_inr: Rs 2 crore of traded value. No phrase fires on a stock nobody can trade. The universe is already liquidity-screened -- p10 turnover was Rs 4.9 crore on 2026-10-16 -- so this removes only the 13 genuinely thin names, not ordinary mid-caps. Rs 5 crore would have cut 79.
thresholds._min_sector_size: Before 'one of the few up in a sector that fell' is allowed. With seven members that is not an observation, it is arithmetic. Ten excludes DEFENCE (7) and TELECOM (8) and keeps REALTY (13) upward.
thresholds._min_history_for_month: Three times the 20-session window. Naming something a one-month high the stock needs history meaningfully longer than a month, or the sentence really means 'near its all-time high'. HEGAM, six weeks listed, is suppressed by this.
thresholds._min_history_for_year: A full 52 weeks. NSE trades about 246 sessions a year, so 240 is the shortest history that honestly supports the words 'a 52-week high'. An earlier draft used 200, and the live data showed why that was wrong: LENSKART, PIRAMALFIN, GROWW and TMCV all sit between 233 and 236 sessions -- roughly eleven months old -- and at 200 the tape would have told a reader a recent listing was at a 52-week high when the stock has not existed for 52 weeks. Ten symbols fall between the two numbers.
thresholds._range_edge_pct: Within a tenth of the day's range of its high or low.
thresholds._heavy_volume_x: Three times the 20-day average. Twice average is ordinary -- roughly a fifth of sessions clear it -- and a phrase that fires on a fifth of the market says nothing. Three times is unusual enough to be worth a reader's attention.
thresholds._light_volume_x: Half the 20-day average. The point of the light-volume phrase is that a move happened without participation, and half average is where that stops being noise and starts being the story.

high_52w: at its highest in a year
high_20d: at its highest in a month
low_20d: at its lowest in a month
closed_high: finished at the top of its range
closed_low: finished at the bottom of its range
alone_up: one of the few up in a sector that fell
alone_down: one of the few down in a sector that rose

catch_all._why: A fact that clears its bar with no phrase still reaches the tape, stated plainly. Ugly beats absent: a silently dropped stock is a stock the reader never learns about, and the gap is logged so the vocabulary grows from evidence.
